Title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents exhibit remarkable performance across diverse applications by using external tools to interact with environments. However, integrating external tools introduces security risks, such as indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks. Despite defenses designed for IPI attacks, their robustness remains questionable due to insufficient testing against adaptive attacks. In this paper, we evaluate eight different defenses and bypass all of them using adaptive attacks, consistently achieving an attack success rate of over 50%. This reveals critical vulnerabilities in current defenses. Our research underscores the need for adaptive attack evaluation when designing defenses to ensure robustness and reliability.
Major_Contribution_Result: This paper designs adaptive attacks (including GCG variants such as multi-objective and two-stage GCG, plus AutoDAN where relevant) against eight defenses for indirect prompt injection on tool-using LLM agents. The authors report bypassing all eight defenses with adaptive ASR consistently over 50% on their InjecAgent-based Vicuna-7B and Llama3-8B agent setups, arguing that defense papers need adaptive-attack evaluation.
Research_Limitations_Challenges: Adaptive attacks target only the agent's first-step action; the threat model assumes white-box access to the agent, defense models, and prompts; defenses are attacked individually rather than in combination; and the set of defenses is not exhaustive (e.g., some self-evaluation or alternative finetuning methods are omitted).
Critics: The contribution is red-teaming of existing IPI defenses under white-box adaptive optimization, not a new defense. ASR claims should be read as defense-bypass results on the authors' agent setups (and a smaller AgentDojo subset) rather than a general ranking of all agent defenses. It does not offer a full secure-development evaluation lifecycle beyond urging adaptive testing.
